findings.evidence: template/docs/engineering/model-routing.md:67 reads "routine/standard work retained only when the standalone parent-only topology prevents a safely contained child writer". The diff adds `balanced-parent` as the default for routine/standard on linked worktrees. The same sentence in docs/engineering/model-routing.md (retained-execution section) was not updated either. Only the plan paragraphs and the route-claude paragraph were edited.
findings.summary: Docs still say routine/standard work is retained only on the standalone parent-only topology, which this change makes untrue.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py `_write_gate_main`: invalid JSON, a missing `tool_input.file_path`/`notebook_path`, a relative path without `cwd`, and any exception from `git rev-parse` or `check_task_write` all return `deny(...)` before the managed-task check. The hook is installed in the integration checkout's settings and matches every Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit call. A malformed payload or an unrelated internal error would therefore block writes everywhere in that session. design.md decision 3 says to "fail closed only inside a managed task".
findings.summary: The write-gate hook denies any Write/Edit if its payload is unexpected, even when the target is not in a managed task. The design says it fails closed only inside a managed task.

findings.evidence: `check_task_write` returns for `PLAN_RETAINED or _has_real_delegation(route)` with no caller identity. A supervisor can run `begin-claude-delegation`, which is self-reported, and then write the code itself. Only the later containment postcheck and early gate see this. The docs mention the shell-write limit but not this one.
findings.summary: The write-time gate cannot tell the supervisor from the delegated child, so once a self-reported delegation is open it allows any write, including the supervisor's own.
